key_insight: Self-supervised pretraining can turn heterogeneous neutrino detector data into a transferable representation that improves event classification, reconstruction, and sample efficiency. In simple terms, models learn the structure of detector signals first, then adapt better to different detector technologies with less labeled data.
problem_solved: Neutrino detectors produce complex, sparse, and highly diverse event data that is expensive to label and difficult to generalize across detector types. This paper tackles the challenge of building AI models that work well across heterogeneous detectors while reducing dependence on labeled examples.
method: Pretrain deep learning models with self-supervised objectives on unlabeled neutrino detector events.
Fine-tune the pretrained models for downstream tasks such as classification and reconstruction.
Evaluate transferability across different detector technologies to test foundation-style behavior.
impact: For AI/ML practitioners, this shows that foundation-style pretraining is valuable beyond vision and language, especially in scientific domains with limited labels. It points to a more data-efficient path for building robust models that transfer across instruments and tasks.
visual_elements: Pipeline diagram showing self-supervised pretraining followed by task-specific fine-tuning

Icons for classification, reconstruction, and transfer learning
paper_title: Towards foundation-style models for energy-frontier heterogeneous neutrino detectors via self-supervised pretraining
paper_authors: Saúl Alonso-Monsalve, Fabio Cufino, Umut Kose, Anna Mascellani, André Rubbia
